claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively homogeneous, single-phase solid-solution microstructure.
Controlled high-temperature pre-annealing will trigger partial phase separation in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The pre-annealing treatment will produce nanoscale Cu-rich precipitates dispersed within a primarily solid-solution matrix.
The Cu-rich nanoprecipitates will be thermally stable in the intended high-temperature sliding regime.
Cu-rich precipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion during sliding.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates increases effective work hardening.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates reduces local microscopic plastic deformation.
The precipitate-containing microstructure impedes grain-boundary sliding and dislocation glide.
Impeded grain-boundary sliding and dislocation glide lead to formation of a mechanically mixed layer.
The mechanically mixed layer improves overall wear resistance at elevated temperatures.
Relative to the as-deposited coating, the pre-annealed coating will have a lower wear rate during high-temperature sliding.
Relative to the as-deposited coating, the pre-annealed coating will show less microscopic deformation, including shallower or less extensive plastic-flow features.
The predicted effects apply during sliding at approximately 600–750 °C under controlled load and speed.
Thermally activated deformation processes are significant in the proposed 600–750 °C operating regime.
The predicted improvements may not occur at lower temperatures because phase separation and significant dislocation-glide barriers are not activated there.
Oxidation and grain-boundary weakening may compete with the proposed precipitate-strengthening mechanism at high temperature.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis characterizes the Cu-rich precipitates as thermally stable, while the uncertainty field states that their stability still requires characterization.
